messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] p99 streaming latency > 12s for service=prefix-cache (us-west-2). SLO breach detected. p95: 1.2s (baseline 600ms), p99: 14s (baseline 4s). Streaming stalls observed for long responses. Auto-escalation to #incidents. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.dev/d/ops/prefix-cache-live
samir.sre: saw this spike on the paging dashboards. p99 tail got worse after the 02:15 deploy. anyone oncall?
jen.ops: i'm oncall. looking now. :eyes:
maria-ml: i can join — we shipped prefix-hash:v2 at 02:10 with the new salt rotation. wondering if the hash change invalidated a bunch of prefix entries.
kevin-sre: running quick metric pull. cache hit-rate (prefix-cache): before deploy ~92% -> now ~38%. eviction rate +700%. KV latencies rising.
jen.ops: confirmed. reproducing low hit-rate on canary keys. huge churn on namespace keys.
samir.sre: ok probable cause = prefix-hash v2 rollout. that would explain mass invalidations -> paging/backpressure cascade -> streaming stalls. we need fast mitigation. options: rollback prefix-hash, force warm-up, or fall back to non-prefetch path.
jordan-support: heads-up: 6 customer reports of streaming timeouts in the last 20m, 2 escalations flagged as P2. customers mostly on large-response endpoints.
jen.ops: mitigation plan: 1) Pause v2 rollout (stop further deploys). 2) Push traffic to stable hash implementation. 3) Backfill hot prefixes (manual key-warm). 4) Short-term increase cache TTL to avoid immediate churn.
maria-ml: agree. quick validation: run this query to compare key distributions:
```
# kdb query
SELECT prefix, count(*) as hits
FROM prefix_metrics
WHERE time > now() - 1h
GROUP BY prefix
ORDER BY hits DESC
LIMIT 20
```
we're seeing many formerly-hot prefixes now cold.
kevin-sre: executing route change to divert read traffic to stable variant now: 
```
# routing command
rctl traffic set prefix-cache --variant stable --percent 100 --env prod
```
I'll run and watch.
jen.ops: also nudged autoscaler to add headroom on prefix-cache pool: `infra scale pool prefix-cache --add 8` (won't fix miss-rate but buys throughput).
kevin-sre: route change applied. 100% -> stable. watching metrics...
incident-bot: (automated) route-change event recorded: rctl traffic set ... by kevin-sre at 5391234620
kevin-sre: hit-rate climbing: 38% -> 71% over 4m. p99 trending down from 14s -> 5.8s. still above SLO but much better.
samir.sre: good. next: warm the hottest prefixes to accelerate recovery. we have a list of top 200 prefixes — i'll run the backfill job.
maria-ml: launching backfill job in small batches to avoid overloading origin: `jobs backfill-prefix --list hot_prefixes_200 --batch 20`
jen.ops: also temporarily extended prefix-cache TTL from 10m -> 45m to reduce churn (done). monitor memory.
kevin-sre: memory increase observed but within safe limits for now. eviction rate decreasing.
jordan-support: new customer reports slowed but no new timeouts in last 10m. escalating customers notified with note: "we rolled back a recent hash change and are warming cache; will update in 30m."
jen.ops: note for postmortem: deployment pipeline allowed a global rollout without staged validation on prefix-hit metrics. we need a canary gating rule.
samir.sre: agreed. immediate action items: - confirm rollback of prefix-hash:v2 across regions - finish warm-up pass - keep autoscaler headroom until p99 below 600ms for 30m - customer comms follow-up.
kevin-sre: rolled back v2 globally at 5391234725. confirmed no v2 instances in prod.
maria-ml: warm-up job progress: batch 1/10 succeeded, batch 2 started. estimated remaining time ~18m.
jen.ops: running light-weight regression check on streaming tails: `tail-check --window 30m --metric p99_streaming_latency` returns downward trend but still noisy.
kevin-sre: p99 now 3.2s. p95 at 580ms. still not fully stable but within SLO for p95. p99 target is 4s, we're below but keep watching.
incident-bot: customer-impact update: 8 reports total, 2 escalations. ticket numbers: RW-8273, RW-8274.
jordan-support: will close out 5 minor reports with the note and keep 2 escalations active until 1:1 with product team.
samir.sre: preparing handoff to night oncall. summary for handoff: cause = prefix-hash:v2 rollout causing cache invalidations and cascading backpressure; mitigation = rollback to stable, traffic reroute, warm-up hot prefixes, TTL increase, autoscale headroom.
oncall-shift2: taking it. thanks for the handover. current state: p99 3.1s, p95 560ms, cache hit-rate 76% and rising, warmup job 4/10. TODOs for next shift: 1) finish warmup, 2) revert TTL to normal once stable, 3) run canary gating rule for prefix-hash rollout, 4) prepare postmortem draft.
samir.sre: noted -- i've created the postmortem draft stub: https://docs.redwood.dev/postmortems/prefix-hash-rollback-5391234567. Add timelines and customer impact.
jen.ops: thumbs up. adding runbook note: gate future hash changes with a 60m canary and require hit-rate >=85% before global.
maria-ml: will investigate why v2 salt caused such high churn; maybe salt selection algorithm wrong for namespace distribution.
kevin-sre: I'll keep an eye on memory/evictions overnight. alert thresholds lowered for next 6h.
jordan-support: sending final customer update now. :) :thumbsup:
oncall-shift2: acknowledged. handing-off channel to oncall. please ping if we see any regressions.
samir.sre: thanks team. closing bridge for now; will reopen if p99 creeps back. :white_check_mark:
